1.explanation:
• lib/dependency-graph/simulator/simulator-test.js: Contains end-to-end tests of the Lantern simulator, showing how it uses serverResponseTimeByOrigin and additional RTT.  
• lib/dependency-graph/simulator/network-analyzer-test.js: Exercises NetworkAnalyzer.groupByOrigin(), which groups data URIs under the “null” origin.  
• lib/dependency-graph/simulator/connection-pool-test.js: Verifies how connection pools are created per origin and how RTT and server times are allocated.  
• computed/load-simulator-test.js: Exercises the computed artifact that wires up the simulator, demonstrating how data URIs get simulated alongside real URLs.  
• audits/network-rtt-test.js and audits/network-server-latency-test.js: Cover the Lighthouse audits that measure RTT and server latency; these use the same underlying simulator behavior and default constants, so they reference DEFAULT_SERVER_RTT and should fail if data URIs aren’t excluded.
1.bug_scenario: In the Lantern load simulator, data‐URI resources are being treated like normal network requests. When NetworkAnalyzer.groupByOrigin() encounters a data: URI, it assigns it the special origin key “null” and then applies the default serverResponseTimeByOrigin (e.g. 30 ms) and default additional RTT to that origin. As a result, data URIs show up in the console.log with nonzero server response time—even though no real network request is made. The screenshot shows a NetworkRequest with protocol “data” being grouped under origin “null” and then logged with additionalRtt=0 and responseTime=30.
